rows.lessonTitle: Calculation drill: clearance and expected fill for a real BOM subset
rows.claim: Minimum vertical barrel fill for through-hole joints, Class 2 and Class 3
rows.riskIfWrong: Every fill-fraction disposition in m08l05, m09l06 and the THT module compares against this one number.

rows.lessonTitle: Calculation drill: clearance and expected fill for a real BOM subset
rows.claim: Documented exception to the vertical fill minimum
rows.riskIfWrong: Decides whether a partially filled barrel is a disposition or a rework.

rows.lessonTitle: Wave defect atlas: bridging, balling, insufficient fill, bypass, lifted lead, blowholes
rows.claim: A 69 % fill fraction is judged against the class minimum, not against 100 %
rows.riskIfWrong: Determines whether a customer asking for 100 % is asking for a deviation.

rows.lessonTitle: Wave defect atlas: bridging, balling, insufficient fill, bypass, lifted lead, blowholes
rows.claim: Wave-soldered joints are judged against IPC-A-610 class criteria
rows.riskIfWrong: Supplies the class vocabulary used by the wave, rework and inspection modules.

rows.lessonTitle: Disposition language: defect, condition and class in workmanship terms
rows.claim: Disposition language: defect, condition and process indicator by class
rows.riskIfWrong: The whole disposition vocabulary of module 7 rests on the current class definitions.

rows.lessonTitle: Application and masking: spray, dip, selective, thickness, cure, repairability
rows.claim: Coating must not obscure joints the class criteria require to be visible
rows.riskIfWrong: Sets the masking map for coated assemblies.

rows.lessonTitle: What residue is and why it matters: ionic residue, SIR, CAF, contact failure
rows.claim: The 1.56 µg NaCl/cm² ROSE figure is a published reference, not a J-STD-001 pass/fail
rows.valueInCourse: 1.56 µg NaCl/cm² per IPC-TM-650 2.3.25; product limit 1.00
rows.riskIfWrong: J-STD-001 removed the ROSE pass/fail; a lesson treating 1.56 as the requirement would misstate the standard.

rows.lessonTitle: Cleanliness verification: ROSE, ion chromatography, particle count, visual
rows.claim: ROSE reference value used with objective evidence rather than alone
rows.riskIfWrong: Same rule as m12l01 from the opposite direction: what replaces the single limit.

rows.lessonTitle: Reading MSL reality: J-STD-033 / J-STD-020 markings, barrier bag, HIC
rows.claim: MSL classes and their floor life at the reference condition
rows.valueInCourse: MSL 1 unlimited, MSL 2 one year, MSL 2a four weeks
rows.editionInCourse: Rev D (read against Rev E text)
rows.riskIfWrong: Feeds every floor-life number in m02 and the m02 case.

rows.lessonTitle: Floor-life accounting: clock start, accumulation, reset rules
rows.claim: Floor life by MSL at 30 °C / 60 % RH
rows.riskIfWrong: The clock-start and reset rules are applied to these values in every MSL case.

rows.lessonTitle: Baking and dry cabinets: when required, conditions by package, records
rows.claim: Floor life by MSL at reference conditions 30 °C / 60 % RH
rows.valueInCourse: MSL 3 = 168 h, MSL 4 = 72 h, MSL 5 = 48 h, MSL 5a = 24 h
rows.riskIfWrong: The m02l04 and m02l06 cases are decided by subtracting these numbers.

rows.lessonTitle: Baking and dry cabinets: when required, conditions by package, records
rows.claim: Dry storage suspends the clock at 5 % RH or less
rows.riskIfWrong: Corrected in this pass from 10 % to 5 %; the 10 % form is retained only as a caveat.

rows.lessonTitle: Baking and dry cabinets: when required, conditions by package, records
rows.claim: User bake is indexed to body thickness AND MSL, split at 72 h of exceedance
rows.valueInCourse: Table 4-1 matrix; 125 °C column 5-16 h up to 1.4 mm
rows.riskIfWrong: A bake recipe quoted from the wrong column either under-dries or damages the part.

rows.lessonTitle: Baking and dry cabinets: when required, conditions by package, records
rows.claim: Carrier tape temperature ceiling for tape-and-reel bake
rows.riskIfWrong: The "9 days at 40 °C" figure drives the m02l04 and m02l06 scheduling answers.

rows.lessonTitle: Case: expired floor life found mid-lot
rows.claim: A 7 % RH cabinet is not compliant dry storage
rows.riskIfWrong: The case turns on 7 % being above the requirement rather than inside a 5-10 % band.

rows.lessonTitle: Heat transfer in the oven: convection, conduction, radiation, zone structure
rows.claim: Classification profile time above liquidus (tL)
rows.editionInCourse: Rev D (read against Rev E text)
rows.riskIfWrong: m06l01 and m06l05 contrast this with the 30-90 s IPC-7530 guidance and the 60-120 s paste window.

rows.lessonTitle: Heat transfer in the oven: convection, conduction, radiation, zone structure
rows.claim: Time within 5 °C of peak (tp) is limited in the classification profile
rows.valueInCourse: tp limit from the classification profile
rows.editionInCourse: Rev D (read against Rev E text)
rows.riskIfWrong: Caps peak dwell as well as peak temperature.

rows.lessonTitle: Alloy systems and profile families: SnAgCu vs SnPb, liquidus basis, nitrogen vs air
rows.claim: Package peak-temperature ceiling by thickness and volume
rows.editionInCourse: Rev D (read against Rev E text)
rows.riskIfWrong: Caps every peak temperature the reflow module sets.

rows.lessonTitle: Area ratio and aspect ratio: definitions, calculation, fine-pitch consequences
rows.claim: Minimum area ratio for reliable paste release
rows.riskIfWrong: Every aperture in m03, m04l01 and the m03l02 calculation is judged against 0.66.

rows.lessonTitle: Aperture calculator and drawing review
rows.claim: Minimum aspect ratio (aperture width / foil thickness)
rows.riskIfWrong: Paired with area ratio on the stencil drawing review.

rows.lessonTitle: Aperture calculator and drawing review
rows.claim: Recommended aperture wall taper
rows.riskIfWrong: A drawing-review acceptance item in m03l05 and m03l06.

rows.lessonTitle: Stencil acceptance, cleaning regime and lifetime tracking
rows.claim: Stencil purchase specification repeats the release criteria
rows.riskIfWrong: The lesson marks these as "based on guidance"; the tension band is supplier practice, not a standard value.

rows.lessonTitle: From aperture to deposit: how stencil geometry becomes paste volume
rows.claim: Area-ratio target applied to chip and QFP apertures
rows.riskIfWrong: The m04l01 calculation reduces a 0.30 mm pad by 10 % and tests it against this number.

rows.lessonTitle: Contact time and fog height: dwell calculation, wave height vs board clearance
rows.claim: Flux solids deposition range for wave soldering
rows.section: flux classification; deposition is supplier data
rows.riskIfWrong: Quoted as a range with a unit-conversion trap; the classification, not the deposition, comes from J-STD-004.

rows.lessonTitle: Solder paste, flux and adhesive receipt: alloy, powder, expiry, cold chain
rows.claim: Solder powder size classes by type number
rows.riskIfWrong: Sets which paste type the fine-pitch lessons call for.

rows.lessonTitle: Bare PCB receipt: surface finish, planarity and warpage, packaging, shelf life
rows.claim: Bow and twist limits come from IPC-6012 by board class
rows.editionInCourse: Rev F (September 2023); the course's cleanliness figure is cited from Rev E §3.9.1
rows.riskIfWrong: The course cites Rev E §3.9.1 for cleanliness while Rev F is current — the exact case the registry exists for.

rows.lessonTitle: Aperture geometry by component: chip, QFP fine pitch, QFN/LGA, BGA
rows.claim: Final aperture values are verified against IPC-7351 land patterns
rows.riskIfWrong: IPC lists 7351 Rev B as current and "no longer maintained"; IPC-7352 (2023) is a separate guideline.

rows.lessonTitle: Profile anatomy: ramp, soak, time above liquidus, peak, cooling — what each controls
rows.claim: Time above liquidus window for a lead-free profile
rows.riskIfWrong: The m06 profiles are judged against this band; IPC-7530 itself gives a wider 30-90 s guidance window.

rows.lessonTitle: Repair limits: IPC-7711/7721 classes, conductor cut, annular ring, laminate damage
rows.claim: Repair limits: conductor cut, annular ring and laminate damage by class
rows.valueInCourse: procedure classes with a permitted-conditions table
rows.riskIfWrong: Written against Rev C (2017); Rev D (January 2024) is current and was not re-read.

rows.lessonTitle: Disposition language: defect, condition and class in workmanship terms
rows.claim: Repair-versus-rework boundary used in disposition
rows.riskIfWrong: A disposition that calls a repair "rework" hides a documented deviation.

rows.lessonTitle: Application and masking: spray, dip, selective, thickness, cure, repairability
rows.claim: Coating types by cured chemistry and their qualification tests
rows.riskIfWrong: Rev C (2019) is current; type UT and SC only exist from Rev C onwards.
